criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal population-level drinking-water service coverage (WC) and wastewater service coverage (WWC) provided by local municipal water and wastewater service (WWS) providers in Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading diverge (passes plain wording = yes; fails narrow rule-type reading = no). Under the plain wording of Criterion 2 ('a legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), participation in and duration of intermunicipal cooperation (IMC, IMCd) through public consortia is clearly an institutional and governance factor in municipal WWS provision, so plain_criterion2_decision is 'include'. Under the active 2026-10-13 A16 clarification, however, Criterion 2 requires a rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership or regulatory structure directly governing service access). Here, utility ownership is held constant by restricting the sample exclusively to municipalities that directly provide WWS and have not delegated service provision to state-owned utilities or public or private companies (p. 4); cost-recovery (FIN) is analysed only as a dependent outcome rather than a tariff rule; and regulatory structures or contractual rules governing household access are not examined (p. 8). Instead, IMC and IMCd measure horizontal inter-municipal collaboration analysed through economies of scale, transaction-cost reduction, and organizational learning in procurement, investment planning, and operational efficiency (pp. 2-3, 8).
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical panel-data econometric study analysing 1,720 municipality-year observations across 344 Brazilian municipalities from 2015 to 2019 using secondary administrative data from IBGE (MUNIC) and SNIS, estimated with fixed-effects, random-effects, and Mundlak correlated random-effects regression models.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipality-level access/coverage outcomes for both water coverage (WC: ratio of served population to total municipal population, %) and wastewater coverage (WWC: ratio of served population to total municipal population, %), alongside financial performance (FIN) and inverse water-loss service quality (QUA).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the unit of analysis and sample (344 Brazilian municipalities directly providing WWS over 2015-2019, N = 1,720), exposures (IMC binary participation indicator and IMCd duration in years, with lnPOP control), outcomes (FIN, WC, WWC, QUA), and econometric panel study design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English, which is directly eligible without translation.

evidence_quotes.quote: The association between IMC and performance is analysed separately across four key dimensions: financial outcomes, water coverage, wastewater coverage, and service quality, measured by water losses.
WC (Water coverage) Measured by the ratio of served population to total population of the municipality

23.4% of the municipalities that directly provide WWS – the focus of the IMC analysis – that is, municipalities that have not delegated service provision to state-owned utilities or to public or private companies.

The data refers to the period 2015 to 2019 and were collected from the Municipal Basic Information Survey (MUNIC), conducted by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE, 2023), and from the National Sanitation Information System (SNIS, 2023).
The empirical analysis employed balanced panel data, characterised as a short panel comprising 344 municipalities observed over five years.
Learning effects may enhance procurement practices, investment planning, and operational efficiency, ultimately translating into improved financial performance and service outcomes.

raw_response.exposure: Participation in horizontal intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) for water and wastewater services through public consortia (binary indicator) and duration of IMC participation in years (IMCd), controlling for log municipal population (lnPOP)
raw_response.outcome: Municipal water coverage (WC, % of municipal population served), municipal wastewater coverage (WWC, % of municipal population served), financial outcome (FIN, operational revenue to total service expense ratio, %), and service quality (QUA, inverse water-loss index, %)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 344 Brazilian municipalities that directly provide water and wastewater services (without delegating provision to state-owned utilities or public or private companies), observed annually from 2015 to 2019 (balanced panel of N = 1,720 municipality-year observations)
raw_response.rationale: Full-text empirical panel study (Ribeiro et al., 2026) matching the record metadata and examining municipal water and wastewater population coverage (WC, WWC) across 344 Brazilian municipalities from 2015 to 2019. The paper satisfies c1, c3, c4, c5, and c6, and would be included under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = 'include') because intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) via public consortia is an institutional/governance arrangement. However, under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2, it is excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure): utility ownership is held constant (all sampled municipalities directly provide WWS without delegating to state-owned, public, or private utilities), no tariff/cost-recovery rule, eligibility/tenure requirement, administrative burden, enforcement mechanism, or regulatory structure directly governing service access is analysed, and IMC/IMCd instead capture horizontal inter-municipal collaboration operating via scale economies, transaction-cost reduction, and organizational learning in procurement and operations. Statistical significance and direction of findings played no role in this decision.
raw_response.study_design: Quantitative longitudinal balanced panel regression study (2015-2019) using municipality and year fixed effects (OLS within), random effects (FGLS), and correlated random effects (Mundlak)
